title: WordPress Service Worker Uses EtherHiding, ClickFix and Steganography to Deploy Amatera Stealer
content_md: The campaign has affected hundreds of WordPress websites . Attackers plant a rogue must-use plugin, named in the format site-helper- , that loads automatically with the site. The plugin registers a malicious Service Worker in a visitor’s browser, allowing the attackers to retain control beyond the initial webpage visit. The Service Worker intercepts page requests, removes Content-Security-Policy headers, and injects malicious JavaScript into HTML pages. It avoids WordPress administrators, logged-in users, /wp-admin , and /wp-login.php pages. This selective filtering reduces the chance that a site owner will notice the infection. WordPress EtherHiding Deploys Amatera The injected script connects to a smart contract on the Base blockchain network. The contract stores the campaign’s payload, including HTML for a fake Google reCAPTCHA page. This technique, known as EtherHiding, allows attackers to keep malicious content outside the compromised WordPress server. Instead of downloading a file directly, the fake CAPTCHA tells Windows users that unusual traffic has been detected.
